cases.quote: The positioning of characters and symbols may vary depending on the following. Is the character width full-width, half-width, or something else?
cases.rationale: §A.8's first row lists U+2014 EM DASH and states no frame for it, while §A.27 lists the same code point with the Remark `proportionally-spaced`. Three of cl-08's six keys — U+2014, U+2025 and U+2026 — are listed twice this way, and the frame (字幅) is the document's own axis between the two listings: it is the first of the six differences §3.9.1 enumerates, and §3.9.2 groups by exactly those differences. This occurrence declares the ideographic frame, so §A.27's row does not describe it and cl-08 is the one surviving listing. The advance is one em here and one em again in `A.8/em-dash/proportional-frame`, which declares the other frame with the identical number, because a proportional EM DASH is commonly exactly one em wide: an implementation that infers the frame from the advance instead of reading the caller's declaration answers both cases the same way and must fail one of them (ADR 0002, ADR 0008).

cases.quote:
used in vertical composition
U+3035 follows this
cases.rationale: §A.8's fourth row lists U+3033 VERTICAL KANA REPEAT MARK UPPER HALF, and its Remarks cell carries two facts at once: a writing-direction restriction and a successor constraint. The successor constraint is the only place any Appendix A table states an ordering between two keys. Neither fact is a class: no other Appendix A table lists U+3033, so cl-08 is the answer in this direction and in the other, and the ordering is a statement about how the mark is written rather than about what class the occurrence is in. The input is the two-mark sequence the Remark describes so that the constraint is satisfied rather than assumed. No `frame` is declared, because the key is listed by one class only and §A.8 states no frame for it: an implementation that requires a frame here is over-constraining its callers, since §3.1.2's five classes — cl-01, cl-02, cl-05, cl-06 and cl-07 — are the only ones where an unstated frame leaves no answer to report (ADR 0018).

cases.quote: Furthermore JIS X 4051 states that it is implementation-defined how to handle characters that are not explicitly mentioned, e.g. whether they should belong to either class or not.
cases.rationale: This is the boundary of cl-08. §A.8's Remarks cell on U+2014 reads `Some systems implement U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR very similar behavior to U+2014 EM DASH` / `処理系によっては，U+2015 (HORIZONTAL BAR)にも，同様の振る舞いを実装しているものもある`, and §3.1.10's first item repeats it in the same words. Both sentences describe what other systems do; neither adds U+2015 to a class. No Appendix A table anywhere lists U+2015, and no compatibility decomposition folds it onto U+2014, so an occurrence of it reaches §3.9.2's implementation-defined case and JLReq decides nothing. Both readings kumihan publishes are recorded below, and neither is cl-08. Note that answering cl-08 here would not contradict JLReq — the quoted sentence leaves the case open — which is exactly why this is `unstated` rather than a case with a forbidden outcome. Two places in the document make the question sharper than the Remark alone. §C.2 note 5 writes the unbreakable dash pair as `EM DASH "―", EM DASH "―"` in its English half — U+2015 twice, under the name EM DASH — while the Japanese half of the same list item writes U+2014, and the note's closing paragraph writes U+2015 in both halves; §3.1.10's Japanese half names EM DASH as U+2014 twice and then writes the double dash as `2倍ダッシュ[――]`, which is U+2015 twice, in the same sentence. §A.8 settles which key is meant, because it is the enumeration: U+2014 is the cl-08 member and U+2015 appears in §A.8 only by name, inside a Remarks cell. That divergence is not recorded in spec/derived/defects.tsv, although it is the same species as the locale divergences that are.

cases.quote: Furthermore JIS X 4051 states that it is implementation-defined how to handle characters that are not explicitly mentioned, e.g. whether they should belong to either class or not.
cases.rationale: The same unlisted key as `A.8/horizontal-bar/ideographic-frame`, on the other frame, where the two published readings of §3.9.2's silence diverge: reading the frame gives cl-27 by §3.2.6's own criterion, and the alternative answers cl-19 unconditionally. The pair is what makes the policy question observable — on the ideographic frame both readings agree and an implementation cannot be told apart by that case alone. Neither reading is cl-08, and no reading in kumihan's policy space produces cl-08 for U+2015: §A.8 names the code point inside a Remarks cell and lists it nowhere.
